subtopics.title: The Layers by Composition — Crust, Mantle, Core

questions.question: The boundary between the crust and the mantle, detected because seismic waves suddenly speed up across it, is the:
The physical state of the mantle is best described as:
options: SOLID silicate rock, with a plastic zone — the asthenosphere — in its upper part that deforms and flows extremely slowly

questions.question: The inner core is SOLID despite being the hottest part of the earth because:
options: It is made of a different metal
It has cooled from the outside in
The pressure there is so immense that it forces the iron to remain solid — pressure, not temperature alone, determines state

questions.question: The earth's magnetic field is generated by:
options: Circulating molten iron and nickel in the LIQUID OUTER CORE

questions.question: Continental crust (sial) compared with oceanic crust (sima) is:
options: Thicker (30–50 km, up to 70 km), granitic, LESS dense (about 2,7 g/cm³) and far older
The same thickness but different colour

questions.question: No ocean floor anywhere on earth is older than about 200 million years because:
options: Oceanic crust is continuously CREATED at mid-ocean ridges and continuously DESTROYED at subduction zones
Oceans only formed 200 million years ago
Older rock sinks under its own weight

questions.question: Where oceanic and continental crust converge, the oceanic plate subducts because:
options: It is DENSER — subduction is buoyancy, not an arbitrary rule

questions.question: A tectonic plate consists of:
options: The LITHOSPHERE — crust plus the rigid uppermost mantle, about 100 km thick, riding on the plastic asthenosphere

questions.question: S-waves cannot travel through liquid because:
options: A liquid has no rigidity to transmit a sideways shear

questions.question: The complete absence of S-waves beyond about 103° from the epicentre proves that:
options: The OUTER CORE IS LIQUID — it is the silence that proves it

questions.question: The P-wave shadow zone between roughly 103° and 143° arises because P-waves are:
options: REFRACTED — bent sharply where they pass from the solid mantle into the liquid outer core, and the size of the ring gives the depth of the core-mantle boundary

questions.question: Which is a SUPPORTING line of evidence for a metallic core?
options: The thickness of the ocean floor
The whole earth averages about 5,5 g/cm³ while surface rocks average only 2,7 — so the interior must be far denser, pointing to metal

subtopics.title: Drawing the Interior in Words — and the Exam Traps

questions.question: Describing any layer of the earth's interior, the fixed order given is:
options: Name, depth range, composition, physical state, one distinguishing feature

questions.question: Which statement corrects the most heavily punished error in this topic?
options: The crust is thicker than the mantle
The mantle is SOLID rock; only the asthenosphere behaves plastically, and even it flows rather than pours — magma exists in localised pockets, not as a global ocean

questions.question: The depth of the core-mantle boundary (the Gutenberg discontinuity) is about:
Which pairing is correct?
options: Continental crust: thin, dense, basaltic, young
Oceanic crust: thick, light, granitic, old
Continental crust: thick, light, granitic, old; oceanic crust: thin, dense, basaltic, young

questions.question: In the avocado model, the skin, the green flesh and the pip stand for:
The butter comparison — fridge-cold butter versus butter that has sat in a Durban kitchen — is used to explain:
options: That the mantle is solid rock, but in one band near the top it is soft enough to ooze very slowly, which is what lets the plates move

questions.question: Why does the hottest place in the earth not melt?
options: It is made of a metal with a very high melting point only
It is cooled from the outside
It is squeezed so hard by everything above it that the iron cannot spread out into a liquid — pressure beats heat
It is not actually the hottest place

subtopics.title: Two Kinds of Raft on One Pool

questions.question: In the swimming-pool picture, the thick polystyrene block and the thin steel sheet stand for:
When the two are pushed together, the steel sheet slides under the polystyrene because:
options: It is DENSER — and that is subduction, which is why the great ocean trenches sit right against continents

questions.question: The Kaapvaal Craton beneath much of northern South Africa is offered as an example of:
options: One of the oldest surviving pieces of continental crust anywhere on the planet

questions.question: 'Crust is the skin; the plate is the skin with a layer of flesh still attached' means:
options: The plate is thinner than the crust
Plates are made of ocean water
The crust and the plate are the same thing
A plate is the crust PLUS the rigid top slice of the mantle — about a hundred kilometres of solid rock sliding on the soft layer below

questions.question: The 'knock' we use to explore the earth's interior is:
options: An earthquake, with thousands of seismic stations as the ears

questions.question: The rope-and-water comparison explains that:
options: Sideways shaking travels along a rope but not through water, because liquid has no rigidity — which is why S-waves die in the outer core
Both waves stop at the Moho

questions.question: P-waves are said to bend 'the way a straw looks broken where it enters a glass of water'. That bending:
options: Leaves a quiet ring on the surface whose size tells us exactly how deep the core starts

questions.question: Which is NOT one of the three backing clues given?
options: The whole earth weighs far more per bucket than surface rocks do
A compass works, and only sloshing liquid metal can make a magnetic field
Iron meteorites look like the cores of smashed-up planets
Volcanoes erupt liquid rock, proving the mantle is a global ocean of magma
